results.title: UW-Eau Claire chancellor’s inauguration set for Nov. 20
results.description: UW-Eau Claire chancellor’s inauguration set for Nov. 20 olsondc Published on: November 16, 2026 ID Authored on Share this story: Intro text The University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire will celebrate the inauguration of Chancellor Edwin A. Martini at 1 p.m. Friday, Nov. 20, in the Ojibwe Ballroom of the W.R. Davies Student Center. Martini began serving as UW-Eau Claire's ninth chancellor on July 1. He brings more than two decades of public higher education experience to the role, most recently in positions leading significant institutional transformations at UW-Oshkosh and Western Michigan University. Visit the chancellor’s webpage for more of Martini’s biography. Sections In addition to Martini’s inaugural address, the ceremony will include remarks from the following distinguished guests and campus leaders: Mary F. Hoffman, interim provost and vice chancellor, presiding Kyle Weatherly, Universities of Wisconsin Board of Regents president Brian McInness, Heather Ann Moody and Marcia St. Germaine, welcome from tribal nations and land acknowledgement Kelly Murray, Nicole Owen and Isabelle Shepard, UW-Eau Claire shared governance leaders Personal reflections by Kyan and Cassidy Martini-Zeller, children of Edwin Martini and Genanne Zeller Keynote address from Jeff “Frenchy” Morisette, Martini-Zeller family friend Renée M. Wachter, interim president of the Universities of Wisconsin, investiture of the chancellor Morisette, who adopted a nickname once used by his grandfather from Montreal, has known Martini since graduate school days. He holds a Ph.D. in forestry from North Carolina State University and spent his career performing academic research for federal government agencies. Morisette will focus on the many ways his longtime friend embodies UW-Eau Claire’s guiding values, and how Martini’s background as a historian will serve him well throughout his tenure as chancellor. Morisette’s remarks will share, in part, that, “Ed’s work exhibits a diligence in exploring critical underlying factors of complex situations and requires keen cultural sensitivity. Throughout his career, Ed has exemplified the importance of listening, and history shows that will serve him well in this role.” Music throughout the ceremony will be performed by students from UW-Eau Claire’s Wind Symphony, Women’s Concert Chorale and The Singing Statesmen. A reception will immediately follow the ceremony in the Marketplace, located on the first floor of the W.R. Davies Student Center, from 2:30-4:30 p.m. Chamber music during the reception will be performed by UW-Eau Claire students from the music and theatre arts department. More information about inauguration activities, including parking details and links to the live broadcast, can be found on the inauguration webpage. For the media Image download
